status: Design budgets; not full PVT/local-mismatch qualification
basis: Rounded design budgets informed by the historical V2.0.3 SS/SF envelope and V2.1.0 waveform screening. The initial 1200 ps budget missed the SS 16x16 sequence read deadline, so the smallest budget is 1600 ps. Historical fits are not executed at runtime. See docs/design/TIMING_LOOKUP_V2_1_0.md for exact coverage and limits. The initial 512-row budget missed SS distributed read (3.341 ns clock-to-data), so the 512-row budget is 3600 ps. V2.1.3 adds a separate budget for 10T cells: the V2.1.2 follow-up (docs/design/TIMING_FOLLOWUP_V2_1_2.md) found the shared 1600 ps class failing 16x16 10T with a column mux nominally and 8x4 under mismatch at SS 0.9 V / 125 C, and the V2.1.3 evidence run found the 16x16 10T sequence without a mux failing the same read-output checks; the 10T read port and the mux pass gate cost about 170 ps and 140 ps of the access window. The first evidence pass at a flat 200 ps above the shared classes failed the 128x8 10T mux read at 5.5 ns (output 40 ps before the deadline) and left only 125 ps at the 32x16 bound at 4.5 ns, so the 10T row budget grows with height and keeps at least 250 ps at every class bound; the 512-row class additionally needs the 10T read-disturb bump on the storage node to decay within the 0.1 VDD tolerance, which failed at 11 ns. See docs/design/TIMING_10T_BUDGET_V2_1_3.md for the evidence run. V2.1.4 re-evidences both 6T ladders against the same rule after the TIME write-request hold latch (docs/design/TIMING_6T_BUDGET_V2_1_4.md): at SS 0.9 V / 125 C nominal the shared classes left 109 ps at the 32x16 6T read bound at 4 ns, 206 ps at 64x16 at 4.5 ns, 203 ps at 128x8 at 5 ns and 175 ps at 256x4 at 6 ns, so the shared row budgets become 1800/1900/2100/2500/3600 ps; 6T with a column mux failed the shared read-output checks nominally at 32x16 (38 ps before the deadline), 128x8 (53 ps) and 256x4 (29 ps after it) and two of three mismatch seeds at 16x16, so it has its own variant. V2.1.5 resizes the 10T pull-down stack to 287 nm (docs/design/TIMING_10T_BUDGET_V2_1_5.md): the 10T read-disturb bump that set the 512-row class is the read current through two stacked pull-downs, and the V2.1.3 width was the 6T single-pull-down width, so at SS 0.9 V / 125 C the 512-row storage node was still at 0.100 V at the 11 ns deadline against the 0.1 VDD tolerance. The wider stack leaves it at 0.056 V and also moves the read output about 400 ps earlier, so the 512-row 10T budget becomes 4000 ps (10 ns); the other 10T classes are unchanged and keep more margin than the 250 ps rule requires.
policy: T = ceil_to_50ps(2 * max(row.half_period_ps, column.half_period_ps) * (1 + margin)); default margin 0.25. Round dimensions up to anchors, extrapolate the final geometric ladder beyond them and flag the result. The shared classes apply to every architecture without a variant entry; a variant keyed by cell_type (and mux, when given) replaces both ladders for that architecture and may never fall below the shared budget. Physical wiring still shares the classes; custom RC still requires waveform checks.

variants.basis: Row classes 2000/2200/2400/3200/5600 ps and column classes 200 ps above the shared ladder, with or without a column mux. The 10T read port discharges the replica bitline about 1 ps per row slower than 6T and its sense path adds a near-constant 200 ps, so the row budget grows with height. Rule: at least 250 ps between the local read output and the 1.2 T deadline at the class bound, nominal SS 0.9 V / 125 C (the 4.5 ns class left 125 ps at 32x16 and failed one mismatch seed). The 512-row class was set by the storage node, not the output: the 10T read-disturb bump decays with the bitline, which a 512-row array discharges slowly. V2.1.5 widens the stacked 10T pull-down to 287 nm, which drops the bump from 0.196 V to 0.161 V and the 512-row storage node at the 11 ns deadline from 0.100 V to 0.056 V, so the 512-row class becomes 10 ns instead of 14 ns. 5 ns up to 32 rows / 16 columns, 5.5 ns to 64 rows, 6 ns to 128, 8 ns to 256, 10 ns to 512.

Row classes 1900/2000/2200/2700/3600 ps and the shared column classes, 6T cells with a column mux only. The mux pass gate delays the local read output by about 70 ps at 32 rows, 95 ps at 64, 150 ps at 128, 200 ps at 256 and 275 ps at 512 rows (V2.1.4 probe reads, SS 0.9 V / 125 C nominal), so the shared ladder failed its read-output checks at 32x16 (4 ns), 128x8 (5 ns) and 256x4 (6 ns) and two of three mismatch seeds of the 16x16 sequence. Rule as for 10T: at least 250 ps between the local read output and the 1.2 T deadline at every class bound, nominal; sequences need about 50 ps more than reads, hence 4.75 ns up to 32 rows. The 512-row mux read keeps 257 ps at the shared 9 ns class. 4.75 ns up to 32 rows, 5 ns to 64, 5.5 ns to 128, 6.75 ns to 256, 9 ns to 512.
